title: Room.wall_item() bookkeeps wall items as +-size/2 around their origin; 64 of 274 wall models are not centred, so overlaps and over-ceiling items are accepted
evidence: Fuzz (random against_wall / wall_item / run calls on the unfurnished ship, audited with the committed rules; 10 seeds): 21 wall-item-overlap and 3 wall-item-span errors. Minimal case: table_fold_down_table (bounds y -0.04..0.40, mount_y 0.9 -> real extent 0.86..1.30 m) and antenna_feed_horn_panel (y 1.5 -> 1.15..1.85 m) on the same N-wall span were both accepted (engine recorded 0.68..1.12 for the table); pipe_elbow_up (bounds y -0.073..0.97, size 1.043) at y=2.5 in a 3.4 m room reaches 3.47 m but passed the `yy + size/2 > h - 0.02` check.
impact: Wall items could overlap or poke through the ceiling whenever the engine said they fitted; only the recipes' luck kept the committed ship clean. The generator output now differs (1405 placements instead of 1401: a digital message board that was wrongly refused is placed).
fix: Use the model's real vertical extent yy+bounds_min[1] .. yy+bounds_max[1] (tolerance -0.02 below the floor, like the audit) for the ceiling/floor check, the overlap test and the recorded wall_used span.
resolution: Fixed in Room.wall_item. Tests: test_P001_wall_item_bookkeeping_uses_the_real_vertical_extent, test_P001_wall_item_top_is_checked_against_the_ceiling_with_real_bounds, test_P002_engine_and_audit_agree_on_random_wall_placements (fuzz). Committed ship still has 0 audit errors.

title: The engine lets tall floor props stand next to windows; only the audit rule window-blocked (0.5 m) knew about the clearance
evidence: Fuzz, 10 seeds, windows from hull_windows(): 195 window-blocked errors from Room.against_wall / place (e.g. specimen_containment_cylinder 2.23 m tall, 0.39 m from a window; plant_ficus_tree 1.94 m, 0.34 m). against_wall only compares the wall span +-0.1 m, place() never looks at windows.
impact: Any recipe that places a tall prop near a window silently produces an audit failure (or, before the audit existed, a blocked view); the engine and the audit disagreed on what is allowed.
fix: Room records the world segment of every window (window_segs); place() refuses floor props taller than 0.6 m whose footprint is within 0.5 m of one (same constants as the audit, now shared from shiplib: WINDOW_CLEAR, WINDOW_CLEAR_H, seg_poly_dist).
resolution: Fixed in Room.add_window / Room.place. Tests: test_P002_engine_keeps_tall_floor_props_clear_of_windows and the fuzz test above. Committed ship output unchanged by this fix.

title: wall-floor-clash and ceiling-floor-clash have no tolerance: flush items rounded to 1 mm are reported as clashes
evidence: Fuzz: `wall item tank_expansion_tank (lowest point 1.14 m) collides with floor prop loader_hand_pallet_jack (1.14 m tall)` and a clock vs a scrubber with a 0.001 m2 'overlap' although the engine (1 mm tolerance in _vclash / wall_item) accepted them. positions in ship.json are rounded to 1 mm, footprint-overlap already needs 5 mm depth, these two rules compared with `<=` / `> 1e-6` and an area-only threshold.
impact: False errors (and false confidence: the same rule cannot be both strict and tolerant for the same geometry), so engine-valid layouts fail the audit depending on rounding.
fix: Vertical contact within 2 mm (TOUCH_TOL) is touching, and both rules now use polys_intersect (area > 1 cm2 and depth > 5 mm) like footprint-overlap.
resolution: Fixed in audit.check_room. Test: test_P003_touching_and_millimetre_contacts_are_not_clashes (also proves a real clash still fires).

title: policy.room_key('') raises IndexError (room_id[-1])
evidence: python -c "import policy; policy.room_key('')" -> IndexError: string index out of range; policy.allowed('') and audit.Room for an empty id crash the same way.
impact: A ship file with an empty room id crashes the audit instead of being reported.
fix: room_id.rstrip('0123456789') (identical for every non-empty id).

title: Room.is_circulation() uses startswith(('cor', ...)): the Computer Core ('core') counts as a corridor and escapes the low-density warning
evidence: A('core').is_circulation() -> True; with the lobby renamed 'core' an empty 100 m2 room gets no `density` warning although every other room does.
impact: Rule `density` (very low occupancy) silently skipped for the Computer Core (and any future id starting with cor/lobby/tower/lift).
fix: Match the real circulation ids with a regex ^(cor[FA]|lobby|tower[AB]|lift[A-Z]?)\d*$.

title: A room whose rectangle lies outside the hull crashes with `ValueError: min() iterable argument is empty`
evidence: Room(ship, 'far', 'Far', 1, (100, 100, 110, 110)) with a hull -> clip_convex returns [] -> ValueError from min(xs) with no room id.
impact: Typo'd drafting coordinates give an unrelated stack trace.
fix: Raise ValueError naming the room, its rectangle and the deck when the clipped polygon has < 3 points.

title: light_grid(shadow_every=0) divides by zero
evidence: R.light_grid(shadow_every=0) -> ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero (k % shadow_every); spacing<=0 also divides by zero / makes nx explode.
impact: A documented-looking parameter value crashes the generator; no way to say 'no shadows' or 'all shadows'.
fix: shadow_every is clamped to >= 1 (1 = every light casts a shadow); spacing <= 0 raises a clear ValueError.

title: Room.grid() with a tuple of families places nothing (silently); arc() with its default cats=None raises TypeError
evidence: R.grid(('crate', 'barrel'), 1, 1, 9, 9, 3, 3) -> 0 placements (the tuple is wrapped as [('crate','barrel')], no such family); dressing.arc(R, 5, 5, 2, 0, 90, 3) -> TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable. row() accepted tuples, grid() only lists, arc() neither.
impact: A recipe author passing a tuple gets an empty BOM line with no error (the audit only notices after the fact).
fix: One normaliser shiplib.as_cats() (str/tuple/list/set -> list, empty -> ValueError) used by grid, arc and row.

title: Ship.link() accepts any `kind`: a typo ('doors') silently becomes a 4 m wide open arch without a door
evidence: ship.link('a', 'b', kind='doors') returns normally; w/h fall back to the 'open' defaults (4.0 x 3.0) and no door model is added.
impact: Mis-spelt link kinds produce wrong openings and a missing door instead of an error.
fix: Reject kinds other than door/portal/open with a ValueError.

title: Floor occupancy is computed three different ways: rugs, floor markings and door frames count in BOM.md and on the room sheets but not in the audit's `density` rule
evidence: Hangar: BOM.md / room plan print 61 % (above the rule's 60 % error line) while rule density measures 25.1 %; cargo 25.4 % vs 24.3 %; lounge 16.6 % vs 15.8 % (door frame counted). audit_stats() and shipmodel.Room.occupancy() summed every floor prop, the rule skips flat props (<= 15 cm) and door frames.
impact: The documents contradict the audit; the hangar looks overfull (61 %) although it is 25 % occupied.
fix: audit_stats, shiplib.Room.occupancy and shipmodel.Room.occupancy use the density definition (non-flat floor props, no door/doorframe).

title: opening-validity ignores the height range: a window 9 m tall or with y0 >= y1 passes
evidence: Mutation: window {y0: 0.5, y1: 9.0} in a 3.0 m room, and {y0: 2.0, y1: 1.0}: audit reports nothing (only density warn).
impact: A mistyped window/door height is invisible to the audit but cuts a hole through the ceiling slab in the game.
fix: Require -0.01 <= y0 < y1 <= room height + 0.01 and width > 0.
resolution: Fixed. Test: test_P011_opening_heights_are_validated (and the rule matrix).

title: ship['doors'] is not audited at all: unknown door model, missing room or a door standing where no opening exists all pass
evidence: Mutations: door model 'nodoor'; door at (3, 3); door joining a room that does not exist -> no violation (only unknown models of room props were checked).
impact: bom.py / the game crash (KeyError) or place a door in a solid wall; rule `unknown-model` could not catch it.
fix: New rule `ship-structure`: door model must be in the catalog (unknown-model), both rooms must exist, and the door must lie on a door opening of room a.

title: door-clearance trusts the generator's zones: an opening whose clearance zone was never reserved is not protected
evidence: Mutation: zones=[] on every room, crate 1.2 m in front of the door: no door-clearance error (the old walkable test even had to wipe the zones to isolate its rule).
impact: A recipe that adds an opening without block_door() lets furniture stand in the doorway unnoticed.
fix: Room.zones() always adds the zones implied by door/open openings (like Room.block_door; hull openings to space excluded), de-duplicated against the written ones.
resolution: Fixed. Test: test_P013_door_zones_are_derived_even_when_the_generator_wrote_none; test_walkable_door_blocked in tests/test_audit.py updated (it now also sees door-clearance).

title: Duplicate BOM line codes in one room are silently merged (dict overwrite)
evidence: Mutation: append a copy of the room's only BOM line -> no violation; bom.room_items then merges the counts so a line is printed twice with the same items.
impact: Two lines with one code attribute props ambiguously in BOM.md and the drawings' balloons.
fix: bom-line rule reports a code used twice.

title: Light entries are never checked: a light outside the room or above the ceiling passes
evidence: Mutation: {'type':'spot','pos':[500,2,500]} and a light at y=99 -> no violation.
impact: Lights floating outside the ship (wasted shadow budget) or underground are invisible.
fix: Rule `lights` checks every light is inside the room polygon (2 cm tolerance) and between floor and ceiling.
resolution: Fixed. Test: test_P015_lights_must_be_inside_their_room (committed ship has 0 such errors).

title: Duplicate room ids and rooms on a deck that is not in the deck list are accepted (floor level silently 0)
evidence: Mutations: deep-copied room (same id) only tripped hull-containment by accident; decks=[{id:2}] with rooms on deck 1 gave no violation (deck_y.get(deck, 0.0)).
impact: ctx.by_id collapses duplicate ids so rules run on the wrong room; a missing deck makes every floor prop 'floating'.
fix: ship-structure rule: unique ids and every room's deck listed (v2 files).

title: A malformed prop crashes the audit (KeyError 'pos' / ValueError cannot convert float NaN to integer) instead of being reported
evidence: Mutations: {'m':'crate'} -> KeyError; pos [nan,0,1] -> ValueError from the grid builder; missing 'm' -> KeyError.
impact: The tool meant to find bad data dies on it, hiding every other finding.
fix: Ctx validates id/pos (finite, 3 numbers) and reports ship-structure, skipping the prop.

title: `audit.py --room typo` prints '0 errors' and exits 0
evidence: python tools/layout/audit.py --room bridg -> '0 errors, 0 warnings', exit status 0 (filter matches nothing).
impact: A mistyped room id in a CI step or a pre-commit check passes forever.
fix: audit(only_room=unknown) raises ValueError listing the rooms; the CLI prints it and exits 2.

title: Several audit rules had no mutation test (aisle-width, duplicates, unknown-model, density low, ship-level rules); a rule could stop firing unnoticed
evidence: Grep of tests/test_audit.py: no test builds a violation for aisle-width, duplicates or unknown-model.
impact: Dead rules go unnoticed (the audit is the safety net of the whole layout).
fix: One mutation per rule of audit.RULES; the test also fails when a rule is added without a mutation or the clean ship stops being clean.
resolution: Added test_P049_every_audit_rule_fires_on_a_minimal_violation (all 30 rules fire). Found no dead rule, but the gaps above were real.

title: Text colour is never applied: `fill` is an attribute but the stylesheet has `.t{fill:#111}`, and CSS beats presentation attributes
evidence: Generated sheets contain 2,761 <text class="t" fill="#..."> elements (grey notes, blue window marks, red zone labels) that all render #111.
impact: Every coloured annotation in the 148 drawings is black; hierarchy and the colour legend are lost.
fix: Emit style="fill:..." (a style attribute outranks the stylesheet).

title: Sheet.render() is not repeatable: it appends the frame and title block to the sheet each call
evidence: render() twice: 8,076 vs 13,272 characters, 'DRAWING TITLE' appears twice.
impact: Any caller that renders a sheet twice (preview + save) gets a doubled frame.
fix: Draw the frame/title block on a copy of the content.

title: dim_v(): both branches of `if y2 - y1 >= w + 0.6` are identical, so vertical dimension text that does not fit is never moved (dim_h has the fallback)
evidence: Source: lines 'self.text(...rot=-90)' appear in both branches; a 2 mm span with a 9-character label is drawn on top of the neighbouring label.
impact: Overlapping dimension text on small rooms/sections.
fix: Nudge via label_rot (up to two steps outwards) and draw anyway when nothing is free (a dimension is never dropped).
resolution: Fixed (label_rot now returns whether it drew). Test: test_P021_vertical_dimension_text_that_does_not_fit_is_nudged.

title: Word wrap emits an empty first line when the first word is longer than the line (two copies of the loop)
evidence: wrap_lines('INTERCONTINENTALLYLONGWORD and more words', 10, 1.7) -> ['', 'INTERCONTINENTALLYLONGWORD', 'and more', 'words'].
impact: Blank lines in the room-purpose block and room labels; a long word gets truncated away on the label.
fix: One svgkit.wrap_words() used by both.

title: crop_png(path, w, h) never crops the width, KeyErrors on palette PNGs, and leaks file handles
evidence: A 7x6 RGB PNG cropped to 4x3 keeps width 7 (`if w < W: w = W`); colour type 3 -> KeyError in {0:1,2:3,4:2,6:4}[ctype]; open(path,'rb').read() and open(path,'wb').write() leave closing to the GC.
impact: Docstring promised 'top-left w x h'; the README screenshot export would break on a narrower window or an indexed PNG.
fix: Real crop with scanline unfiltering (all five PNG filters), unsupported formats return False, files closed.

title: export_png() does not catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired: one hung Chromium aborts the whole drawing build
evidence: subprocess.run(..., timeout=120) raising TimeoutExpired propagates out of draft.main (reproduced by patching run).
impact: --png builds lose all sheets after the first hang.
fix: Catch it, print which PNG was skipped and continue.

title: draft.py --only <unknown room> writes nothing and exits 0
evidence: python tools/draft/draft.py --only bridg -> '0 sheets -> docs/drafts', status 0.
impact: A typo produces an empty (and for CI: passing) drawing run.
fix: argparse error listing the valid room ids.

title: Each stair-tower plan also draws the other tower's flights, 26 m away, outside the sheet
evidence: R-towerA1-P / A2 / A3 contain polygon points at x = 1057.2 / 934.0 mm and the B towers at x = -633.2 / -510.0 mm on a 420 mm sheet (draw_stairs called without only_side).
impact: Extra off-page markup in six sheets; a viewer that shows the whole canvas zooms out to 3x the sheet.
fix: draw_stairs(..., only_side='S' + room.id[5]).

title: G-15 window schedule lists 46 of the ship's 51 windows
evidence: ship.win_list has 51 entries; the table is built from wrows[:46] with maxrows=46, so no '+N more' row appears and the heading says 'WINDOW SCHEDULE (51 panes)'.
impact: Five windows are missing from the schedule that is meant to be the complete list.
fix: Pass all rows; the table shows '+N more' beyond 64 rows (what fits above the title block) and the notes follow the table.

title: Files are opened without being closed or given an encoding; INDEX.md is written without the newline/encoding of the SVGs
evidence: python -X dev tools/draft/draft.py: 'ResourceWarning: unclosed file ... catalog.json' and '... ship.json'; INDEX.md is written with the locale encoding / CRLF on Windows while the sheets use newline='\n', and lacks a final newline.
impact: ResourceWarnings, platform-dependent bytes in docs/drafts/INDEX.md (CI compares the committed drawings).
fix: with-blocks, encoding='utf-8', newline='\n', final newline.

title: A ship without stairs crashes the drawing build with IndexError in the stair-tower sheet
evidence: ship.json with stairs=[] -> draft.main: IndexError: list index out of range (runs[0] in stair_sheet).
impact: No drawings at all for a ship without stair towers (e.g. a one-deck test ship).
fix: stair_sheet returns None when there are no stairs; build_sheets skips it.

title: Every section sheet draws a '4000 F-F' floor-to-floor dimension from a constant `y + 4.0` (`... if room.deck > 1 or True else ''`), also on deck 1 where no floor lies above
evidence: R-bridge-SL contains 'F-F' for a floor that does not exist; the label was a literal and the condition always true.
impact: A dimension to a non-existent level on every deck-1 section; wrong if the deck pitch ever changes.
fix: Dimension to the next deck above taken from the decks list; nothing is drawn on the top deck.

title: G-04/G-05/G-0x sheets hard-code the beam (13 m, 'BEAM 26000') and the deck pitch ('4000')
evidence: Scaling the hull x by 2 and moving the decks to y = 0/5/10 still prints 'BEAM 26000' and the chain labels '4000', and positions the plan at x = 13 m.
impact: The drawings stop matching ship.json as soon as the hull or deck pitch changes, though they claim to be generated from it.
fix: Beam, offsets and the level chain come from ship.bounds()/ship.decks; floor_to_floor() helper for the facts table.

title: bill_of_materials.csv omits every door and doorway frame: 1,368 of the 1,401 placed items
evidence: sum(qty) = 1368 while BOM.md says 'Placed items 1401' (1,375 props + 26 doors); 26 sliding doors and 7 ARCH frames have no CSV row.
impact: The machine-readable bill of materials under-counts what has to be bought/installed.
fix: Rows for frames (bom_line ARCH), doors (DOOR, listed with the first room of the pair) and unassigned items ('-').

title: A prop without (or with an unknown) BOM line is listed as a 'Doorway frame' in the room chapter
evidence: room_items(): `if b == 'ARCH' or b not in lines: arch[...]`; the architecture table then prints 'Doorway frame | <any model> | n'.
impact: A recipe bug (item placed outside any line) turns into a plausible-looking but wrong line of the document.
fix: room_items returns a third group `loose`; the chapter lists it as 'Items not assigned to a BOM line' and the CSV as bom_line '-'.

title: BOM.md states 'every point of every deck is within 35 m of a stair tower' while its own table shows 35.4 m for the armory and brig, rounded to '35 m'
evidence: egress_table(): Armory 35.43 m, Brig 35.43 m (formatted %.0f -> '35 m'); the design limit is 35 m.
impact: A false safety claim in a generated document.
fix: The statement is generated from the table (longest room, count over the limit); rooms over the limit are marked '**over the limit**' and shown with one decimal.
resolution: Fixed (the layout itself is room-content and not touched: two rooms genuinely exceed the limit by 0.4 m). Test: test_P031_escape_statement_matches_the_table.

title: Hard-coded text in BOM.md: '1000 Blender models', '140+ sheets', 'Decks | 3 (floors at +0.0, +4.0, +8.0 m)', the hull from hull.py instead of ship.json, `for d in (1, 2, 3)`
evidence: bom.generate on a ship.json with the hull x doubled still prints 'Beam | 26 m'; on a two-deck ship it raises KeyError 3; the mermaid box says 1000 models for any catalog.
impact: The document that claims 'everything comes from the same data the game is built from' can contradict it.
fix: Counts and decks come from the ship/catalog being documented; hull taken from ship['hull'].

title: bom.load() leaves two file handles to the GC; BOM.md/CSV are written with the locale encoding
evidence: python -X dev tools/layout/bom.py -> ResourceWarning: unclosed file ... ship.json / catalog.json.
impact: ResourceWarnings; platform-dependent bytes in the committed docs/BOM.md.
fix: with-blocks; utf-8 and newline='\n'.

title: `generate_ship.py --decks 3` overwrites godot/data/ship.json with a ship whose other decks are empty
evidence: The default --out is godot/data/ship.json for every invocation; --decks only controls which decks are furnished, so `--decks 1` writes a 1-deck-furnished ship over the game data (the comment says it is for authors iterating).
impact: One careless developer command ships a half-empty game.
fix: --decks requires an explicit --out (argparse error otherwise); main(argv) is testable; bad deck lists are reported.

title: BUGS.md says 'the new layout's remaining entries are warnings only' even when the audit reports errors
evidence: The sentence is a fixed template over the warn entries; with new errors it would still read 'warnings only' (precedence of `... % join if new else ...`).
impact: The ledger can certify a failing layout.
fix: remaining_text() names errors explicitly and only says 'warnings only' when that is true.

title: preview_room: colour per family depends on draw order and cycles after 20 families; unknown room ids are ignored; an id without '_' raises IndexError; files are not closed
evidence: color_for(cat, cache={}) assigns palette[len(cache) % 20] on first use, so the same family has different colours in different runs and the 93 catalog families share 20 colours; `--room typo` with a valid second room silently draws one panel.
impact: The legend promised by the docstring ('colour = family') is meaningless; typos are swallowed.
fix: family_colors(): stable, unique colour per sorted family; unknown rooms exit with a message; split('_', 1)[-1]; with-blocks.

title: inspect_room.py runs argparse and reads ship.json at import time, ignores unknown room ids (exit 0, no output) and leaks a handle
evidence: `python tools/layout/inspect_room.py nosuchroom` prints nothing and exits 0; importing the module with other argv exits via argparse.
impact: Not importable/testable; typos look like an empty room.
fix: main(argv) with a __main__ guard; unknown rooms listed on stderr, exit 2.

title: save(..., peak=...) divides by np.abs(x).max(): a silent clip gives NaN, and the int16 cast of NaN is undefined
evidence: save(d, 's', np.zeros(100), peak=1000) emits two RuntimeWarnings ('invalid value encountered in divide / cast'); NaN -> int16 is platform-defined (-32768 on x86, a full-scale click).
impact: A degenerate parameter set would write a full-scale burst instead of silence.
fix: Write zeros when the clip's peak is ~0.

title: generate() returns sorted(os.listdir(out)): the printed 'wrote [...]' lists files that were not written
evidence: generate(dir_with_readme) -> ['door.wav', ..., 'readme.txt'].
impact: Misleading output; a stale sound file looks freshly generated.
fix: Return only the names this module writes (WRITTEN).

title: No-op expression statements and constant conditions left in the tools: `g['sgn']`, `za_c = ... if False else ...`, `if d > 1: pass`, `ex += (cx - ex) * 0.0`, `6.4 - 1.5 if True else 0`, a dead list literal in egress_table, `r.w * s`, `sv.xy(a, 0)[0] - 4`, `runs[1]['flights'][0]`, `(14.0, 8.0, 232.0, 290.0)`, `0`, `{}`, `t * e['len'] if True else 0`, `p.mount != 'ceiling' or True`, a dead double assignment of `ox`
evidence: AST scan of tools/ finds 20 such statements outside recipes_deck*.py (generate_ship 4, bom 2, dressing 1, sheets_ga 4, sheets_misc 4, planview 3, sectionview 2).
impact: Dead code hides real intent (what was `if False` meant to disable?) and misleads readers; none changed behaviour.
fix: Removed; recipes_deck*.py (room content) were not touched.
resolution: Fixed. Test: test_P040_no_noop_statements_or_constant_conditions_in_the_tools (AST scan, constant conditions and constant bool operands too).

title: Remaining json.load(open(...)) / open(...).read() sites left to the garbage collector
evidence: AST scan of tools/ for open() outside `with`: 9 sites before the round (shipmodel 2, bom 2, draft 2, inspect_room, preview_room 2).
impact: ResourceWarning under python -X dev, handle leaks on PyPy/Windows.
fix: All converted to with-blocks (fixes listed in P028, P033, P036, P037, P023).

title: deck-1 tops() decides 'host quarter-turned' with yaw % 180 < 1: a host at yaw -0.4 (179.6 after the modulo) is treated as rotated and the items are spread by the host's depth
evidence: -0.4 % 180 == 179.6 -> `else` branch -> w = fp depth (0.5 for a 2.0 x 0.5 host): offsets are +-0.0875 m instead of +-0.35 m.
impact: Table items bunched in the middle of any host whose yaw is a small negative number (or >= 1 degree away from 180).
fix: abs(yaw) % 180 within 45..135 -> quarter turn.
resolution: Fixed (output unchanged: no committed host has such a yaw). Test: test_P042_deck1_tops_measures_the_host_width_for_tiny_negative_yaw.

title: chairs_around(ends=True) turns the two end chairs away from the table
evidence: Chair at x = cx - (hw + 0.4) gets yaw -90 (front vector (-1, 0)) and the one at the +X end gets +90, i.e. both look outwards; the side chairs are right.
impact: Any recipe using the end chairs would seat people with their backs to the table (cf. B056-B058).
fix: yaw +90 for the -X end, -90 for the +X end.
resolution: Fixed (helper currently unused, so the committed ship is unchanged). Test: test_P045_end_chairs_face_the_table.

title: Ship.link() on an empty/incomplete catalog raises TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable (pick(...) returns None) and an unknown door model raises a bare KeyError
evidence: generate_ship.build() with a catalog of zero models -> TypeError in link(); link(..., model='x') -> KeyError 'x'.
impact: Edge input (empty catalog) gives an unreadable error; the generator should say which model family is missing.
fix: ValueError naming the missing 'door'/'doorframe' family or the unknown model.

title: Two invariant tests are far weaker than their names: 'props inside their room' allows 0.4 m outside; 'no unreachable pockets' allows up to 4
evidence: A prop 0.3 m outside the west wall line still passes `_inside(poly, x, z, -0.4)`; the committed layout has exactly 3 pockets (airlock, cabinB, life), so a new pocket in any other room (or a second in one room) passes `<= 4`. test_walkable's docstring also says 0.30 m capsule while the audit uses 0.32.
impact: Regressions in two of the main layout guarantees go unnoticed.
fix: props_outside() with margin 0.1 m (door frames -0.01); an allowlist of the three known rooms, one pocket each; docstring corrected.
